evals.prompt: I need a hero image for a blog post about email deliverability. Make it visually striking.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should recommend AI generation as the approach for a one-off blog hero. Should propose a visual metaphor concept that represents email deliverability (e.g., letters being sorted through a maze, signals breaking through a wall, an inbox glow). Should specify 1200x630 (works for both hero and OG image). Should recommend Flux or Gemini for photorealistic, or Ideogram if text in image is needed. Should provide a prompt following Subject + Setting + Style + Lighting + Composition + Technical pattern. Should mention WebP optimization (target <200KB, JPEG fallback). Should not suggest using AI for product UI screenshots.
assertions: Recommends AI generation for one-off hero

evals.prompt: Generate me an image of our app's dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to use AI generation for product UI screenshots and explain why: models hallucinate interfaces, the result won't match the real UI. Should recommend the Product Mockups & Screenshots workflow: capture real screenshots of the product at 2x resolution, frame in device mockups (browser frame, laptop, phone), add callout arrows or feature labels for context, programmatically overlay annotations with Hyperframes or HTML/CSS. Should suggest tools: browser DevTools screenshot, Shottr, CleanShot X, or screencapture CLI. Should warn this is Common Mistake #1: using AI for product UI.
assertions: Refuses to use AI generation for product UI
Notes this as a common mistake

evals.prompt: Need a Twitter/X header banner for our company. We just want to show our product and tagline.
evals.expected_output: Should specify Twitter/X header dimensions: 1500x500 (3:1 aspect ratio). Should warn the banner is partially obscured by the avatar — center critical content and avoid important elements near the avatar overlap area. Should recommend keeping text minimal (seen at small sizes on mobile). Should suggest design tools (Canva or Figma) over AI generation since brand consistency matters. Should recommend Ideogram if heavy text rendering is needed since other AI models butcher text. Should suggest using brand colors + tagline + optional product shot. Should remind to test at actual display size by zooming out.
assertions: Suggests Canva or Figma over AI

evals.prompt: I need 5 versions of the same hero image for Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram feed, Instagram stories, and Facebook. What's the fastest way?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend the Canva Magic Resize workflow over generating 5 separate images. Should list dimensions: Twitter/X 1200x675 (16:9), LinkedIn 1200x627 (1.91:1), Instagram feed 1080x1080 (1:1 — note 1080x1350 / 4:5 also strong), Instagram Stories 1080x1920 (9:16), Facebook 1200x630 (1.91:1). Should explain workflow: create the hero concept at highest resolution needed, use Canva Magic Resize for variants, manually crop if needed, add text overlays programmatically if required (Ideogram or post-processing), export at each platform's specs. Should note this is what Canva Magic Resize is specifically designed for.
assertions: Suggests programmatic text overlays for variants

evals.prompt: What's the best image format for our website?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend WebP as the default choice with JPEG/PNG fallback. Should explain the format guide: WebP for photos and graphics (lossy + lossless, ~96% browser support), AVIF for highest compression (~94% support, newer), JPEG as universal fallback (lossy only), PNG for transparency and screenshots (lossless, universal), SVG for logos and icons (vector, scales, universal). Should reference the optimization checklist: resize to display size, compress (target quality 75-85% for photos), lazy load below-the-fold, set explicit width/height attributes (prevents CLS), use a CDN with auto-optimization (Cloudflare, Vercel, Imgix, Cloudinary), add descriptive alt text. Should provide a quick cwebp or mogrify command. Should note skipping image optimization is the #1 page speed killer.
assertions: Mentions explicit dimensions to prevent CLS

evals.prompt: We're a SaaS that just launched. Need OG images for every blog post we ship — about 2 per week. Doing it manually is killing us.
evals.expected_output: Should recommend Dynamic OG Images programmatic approach. Should explain options: Vercel OG (@vercel/og) generates images at the edge using JSX — best for programmatic SEO since you can dynamically pull post title, author, image into a template; Satori converts HTML/CSS to SVG (powers Vercel OG); Cloudinary for URL-based text overlay on template images. Should explain you build the template once with your branding then it generates unique OG images per page using post metadata. Should mention required meta tags: og:image (1200x630), og:image:width, og:image:height, twitter:card summary_large_image, twitter:image. Should note this is best for programmatic SEO.
assertions: Names Vercel OG, Satori, or Cloudinary
Notes this is best for high-volume blogs

evals.prompt: For [ABC] (kitchen and bath remodeler): generate a before-and-after of a kitchen remodel with our crew standing in the finished kitchen. We'll use it on our Google Business Profile and Instagram this week.
evals.expected_output: Should read bml/context-rules.md and the staged page 13 first and check the scope table for the social/GBP service. Should refuse to generate an AI before/after or any image presented as the client's real project, and refuse to generate the crew (real, identifiable staff) unless written consent is recorded on J-6 and they are named on B-12. Should check approved ClickUp `asset` records and the G-6 photo library / A-17 brand assets before anything else, and check J-6 for project and staff photo permissions; if J-6 is not APPROVED or PROVISIONAL, mark [NEEDS PROOF: J-6] rather than use the photos. Should say GBP photos must be real photos of the business, never AI or stock, and recommend a shoot (G-6, I-8) if no approved photos exist. Should not post to GBP or Instagram, and should draft (not create) the ClickUp task. Should end with the context footer.
assertions: Refuses AI before/after and AI images presented as real projects
Does not generate the crew's likeness without written consent on J-6 and the crew named on B-12
Checks approved asset records and G-6/A-17 before generating
Checks J-6 permission and uses [NEEDS PROOF: J-6] when missing
GBP uses real business photos only
Does not post or publish; drafts ClickUp record only

evals.prompt: [XYZ] is an imaging center. Make a blog hero for 'What to expect at your first MRI' — a smiling patient in the scanner, with 'Rated #1 imaging center — 5 stars' across the top. Photorealistic please.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the clinical segment rules. Should not depict a patient in a way that implies a real patient or outcome, and should offer an approved premises/equipment/process photo from G-6 or a non-patient illustrative alternative. Should treat the overlay text as copy: '#1' and '5 stars' only if APPROVED rows support them (G-1, G-2, A-7, with confirm-before-publishing), otherwise [NEEDS PROOF: <row>] in the spec and the claim left off the rendered image; check page 12 and J-3. Should read J-5 before any AI generation and, if J-5 is not APPROVED or PROVISIONAL, keep client-facing output illustrative, allow photoreal only as a labeled internal preview, list J-5 as a gap and ask before anything client-facing. Should not generate a photorealistic AI person for a clinical client. Should not offer a digital twin or AI likeness of a real patient or staff member, even with consent on file. Should use page 02 brand style, specify 1200x630, and deliver to the router-mapped Drive folder with a spec sheet, never a local ~/ path. Should end with the context footer.
assertions: Does not generate an image implying a real patient
No photorealistic AI people for the clinical client
No digital twin or AI likeness of a real person for the clinical client, consented or not
Does not render unsupported '#1' or star-rating claims; uses [NEEDS PROOF]
Checks J-5 before generating; if not APPROVED/PROVISIONAL, photoreal only as an internal preview, J-5 listed as a gap, asks before client-facing use
Delivers to router-mapped Drive folder with a spec sheet

evals.prompt: [ABC] needs three organic Instagram graphics for a spring promo: '15% off all deck builds — book online today'. Use Canva and whatever image AI you like; I can paste my Ideogram API key if you need it.
evals.expected_output: Should check the scope table for social. Should decline the API key and ask which tools are connected instead. Should use the Figma connector for templates rather than Canva (authorised but not in use) and treat Ideogram as 'if BML or the client has an approved account', and before any paid generation state tool, image count and cost and wait for the user's go-ahead in the conversation. Should check approved asset records and A-17 before generating. Should verify the offer against D-11/D-7 (and D-4 for price wording), the season and capacity against B-6/I-10, and 'book online' against I-9 and page 01's required CTA language; anything missing becomes [NEEDS PROOF: <row>] in the spec, not on the graphic. Should specify 1080x1350 or 1080x1080 sizes, deliver files plus a spec sheet to the router-mapped folder, draft a ClickUp task tagged social (not create it), never post, and end with the context footer.
assertions: Declines the API key and asks about connected tools
Stops for the user's go-ahead (tool, count, cost) before any paid generation
Checks the CTA against I-9 and page 01
Drafts a ClickUp task without creating it and does not post

evals.prompt: For [ABC]: I need a set of Meta ad images for the fall campaign, and a cover graphic for the monthly performance report deck we send them.
evals.expected_output: Should route the Meta ad images to ad-creative (which owns paid ad concepts, copy, ad specs and testing), offering to apply this skill's BML rules if ad-creative hands over a render step. Should treat the report cover as an agency artifact: Baker house style, not the client's page 01 voice or page 02 style, and no client voice loaded. Should not invent claims or figures on the cover. Should mark distinctiveness n/a for the agency artifact, save to the router-mapped folder rather than a local path, and end with the context footer.
assertions: Routes paid ad images to ad-creative
Treats the report cover as an agency artifact in Baker house style
Does not load client voice for the agency artifact
Marks distinctiveness n/a for the agency artifact
Saves to a router-mapped folder, not a local path
